belief: I should be able to handle this on my own.
origins: Self-reliance is praised, and asking for help can feel like failure. Some learned early that no one would help, so they learned to cope alone. Pride and fear of burdening others also play a part.
teaches: God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone.” “Two are better than one.” Paul writes, “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” “He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.” Jesus invites, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” Even Jesus asked friends to watch with Him. We were made for interdependence. Needing help is not failure. It is how God designed us.
self_statements: I should be able to manage.
I do not want to burden anyone.
I have always handled things alone.
If I need help, I have failed.
errors: Believing I must be fully independent or a failure.
Feeling that needing help is shameful.
questions: Where did I learn to handle things alone?
Would I consider someone who asks for help weak?
Who has helped me before, and how did they feel?
What would I do if a friend were in my situation?
What does Scripture say about bearing burdens together?
What is one small request I could make this week?
truth: God made me for community. Needing help is part of being human, and receiving help blesses both sides. I can lean on God and on trusted people.
hw_truths: It is not good to be alone.
Jesus invites the weary to come.
log: Each week, note one time you asked for or accepted help.
actions: Write how you handle things alone.
Come to Jesus with your burden.
prayer: Lord, I have carried this alone. Thank You for making us for each other. Help me ask, receive, and lean on You and on those You send. Amen.
hw_questions: What would I tell a friend?
name_example: Sarah can write: “We carry one another’s burdens, so I can ask for help.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I should be able to handle this on my own.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
